thread.title: Mayor Sheffield appoints Jamie Kaye Walters as senior director of communications
thread.title_full: Mayor Sheffield appoints Jamie Kaye Walters as senior director of communications

author: G. G. Haynes
title: Mayor Sheffield appoints Jamie Kaye Walters as senior director of communications
text:
Mayor Mike Duggan, City of Detroit | City of Detroit website
Mayor Mike Duggan, City of Detroit | City of Detroit website
Jamie Kaye Walters has been appointed as Senior Director of Mayor’s Office Communications by Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield. Walters, a former Local 4 program director and co-founder of the communications agency VVK PR + Creative, will oversee communications strategy for the mayor's office. Her responsibilities include developing messaging that supports key city programs and strategies, with an aim to attract partnerships and foster growth in Detroit.
Walters brings over 20 years of experience in strategic communications, crisis management, and executive leadership. She previously worked at WDIV Local 4, where she managed a team of 34 people and produced major Detroit events such as America's Thanksgiving Parade and Ford Fireworks. She also has experience producing political programming like the show Flashpoint. Walters is a long-term Detroit resident with extensive connections across media, nonprofit organizations, and municipal sectors.
Mayor Sheffield stated: "My administration is going to be about providing all Detroiters with pathways to a better quality of life. We will drastically improve services and make resources available in neighborhoods so that Detroiters stay and raise families here. For our efforts to be broadcasted and utilized, we need to develop creative and innovative ways to communicate to our residents."
She continued: "We also want to bring the Detroiters that moved out of our city with incentives and opportunities, while attracting visitors and major partnerships that support our workforce and small business ecosystem. Elevating our strategies and also our institutions, amenities and unique attractions are top priorities. Jamie’s presence will allow us to think strategically about marketing the Detroit we all know and love to the world. She has spent her lifetime rooted in Detroit and has established herself as one of the most effective and respected communications professionals anywhere. I am proud to have her on our team."
The role of Senior Director of Mayor’s Office Communications differs from departmental communications led by Vickie Thomas. While Thomas oversees messaging for specific departments focused on operations and service delivery, Walters’ position will focus on executive positioning, broad policy messaging, stakeholder relations, and strategic communications aligned with the mayor’s priorities.
This new structure follows common practice in large cities such as Chicago, New York, and Los Angeles. The reorganization is part of Mayor Sheffield’s goal for deeper community engagement while promoting Detroit as a destination for families, economic development, small businesses, and tourism.
Walters said: "When Mayor Sheffield offered me the role, my decision instantly became clear. The chance to work for the people of Detroit and alongside a leader committed to equity, transparency, and real progress was an opportunity I couldn’t turn down."
She will start her new role on Monday, January 26.
